source.title: Adaptive Gradient Method with Resilience and Momentum
source.authors: Jie Liu; Chen Lin; Chu-Ming Li; Lu Sheng; Ming Sun; Jun-Jie Yan; Wanli Ouyang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Compares adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD and reports held-out performance on ImageNet and a language-modeling benchmark, using a different optimizer rather than the versions' original methods.
record.gate_note: The paper's cited claims about Adam and generalization are prior work, not rows. Rows below cover the paper's own optimizer comparisons. It also reports training-loss curves and oscillation measurements; the curves are figure-only, and the oscillation metric is not a measure of the train–test gap.
record.test_reason: The paper's baseline optimizer comparisons directly test V4 through held-out ImageNet accuracy and Penn Treebank perplexity. Its searches also tune momentum and weight decay, so they do not reproduce V4's learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the conclusion: the authors claim AdaRem and AdaRem-S combine fast convergence with held-out performance comparable to SGDM, with AdaRem-S improving ImageNet results on MobileNetV2 and ShuffleNetV2.
record.recipe_differences: Compares a new adaptive optimizer (AdaRem) and other adaptive methods with SGDM on ImageNet and Penn Treebank; uses cosine learning rates for image experiments and grid searches for hyperparameters.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by optimizer and dataset/model: several adaptive methods trail SGDM on ResNet-18/ImageNet, AdaRem matches or nearly matches it, and Adam and AdaRem outperform SGDM on LSTM/Penn Treebank perplexity.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed AdaRem matches SGDM's ImageNet top-1 accuracy and achieves lower Penn Treebank perplexity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AdaRem can match or improve SGDM's held-out performance in the evaluated workloads.

record.problems: The paper does not report uncertainty estimates for the optimizer comparisons. The ResNet-18 train-loss and test-error trajectories are shown as plots without tabulated values. The paper describes grid searches but does not provide a broad-tuning comparison against the cited optimizer study's broader-tuning condition.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. ImageNet architecture comparisons in Tables 1, 5, 6, and 7 compare AdaRem-S with SGDM across models, but are not included because V4 concerns comparisons of adaptive optimizers such as Adam; the ResNet-18 optimizer comparison and Penn Treebank optimizer comparison provide the direct evidence for V4.

untested.parts: Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

The exact learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning regime; a controlled comparison of limited versus broader tuning; switching Adam to SGD; and equal or better training performance of the baseline adaptive optimizers. AdamW is tested, but recovery to SGDM performance is not observed.
Batch-size comparisons and remedies for large-batch penalties.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V4. AdaRem-S results are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing undeclared results. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The oscillation metric does not test V7.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label or natural-label memorization comparison.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.

Tests optimizer comparisons on ResNet-18/ImageNet and LSTM/Penn Treebank. Does not test the cited broader image and language benchmark set, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay as a recovery method, or switching from Adam to SGD.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare generalization measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.

tranche.reason: Independent optimizer comparisons address the same held-out-performance question using a different recipe and broader hyperparameter searches.

source_check.notes: Appendix B.1.1/Table 4 confirms momentum and weight-decay searches, so these results do not isolate learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning. RMSprop's learning rate differs between section 4.1.1 and the appendix; the listed rows specify neither.

statements.correction: ResNet-18/ImageNet top-1 accuracy: AdamW 67.55%; Adam 67.07%; SGDM 70.67%. AdamW improves over Adam but retains an SGDM deficit under this recipe; label: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The study-specific facts are correct, but the challenges label overstates evidence against V4's modal claim that decoupled decay can recover performance.
